best_for: Windows and Mac users who read, mark up, fill and sign PDFs and want a free alternative to Adobe Reader, with an upgrade path if they ever need real editing.

points.title: Read, comment, fill and sign for free
points.text: The free Reader opens, searches and prints PDFs, adds highlights and comments, fills existing form fields and lets you add your signature. Local files open offline.

points.title: Editing is the paid line
points.text: Changing existing text or images, converting to Office formats, OCR and permanent redaction all need Foxit PDF Editor, which has a 14-day free trial.

points.title: No account to read
points.text: Reading, reviewing, form filling and signing work without a Foxit account. A free account is needed only for the AI features.

points.title: AI comes with a monthly allowance
points.text: The AI Assistant can summarize, translate and answer questions about a PDF. A free account gets 300 credits a month, shared with the separate Workspace app. Some text tasks can run on the device on compatible Windows PCs and Apple silicon Macs after a model download.

points.title: Desktop only, no Linux
points.text: The Reader is for Windows and macOS. Phones and tablets use a separate mobile app, and there is no Linux build.

points.title: Installs for all users
points.text: The Windows installer here is x64 and installs machine-wide, so it needs administrator rights. The Mac package is universal and needs macOS 12 or later. The Windows listing keeps 22 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
